questions.question: What is the procedure of secondary treatment of sewage? / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• What is the procedure of secondary treatment of sewage?
  • Trickling filter is used for the secondary treatment of sewage.
  • A trickling filter is a wastewater treatment process that uses a fixed
  • bed of media, like rocks , for aerobic microorganisms to grow on as
  • a biofilm. As wastewater is sprayed over the media, the biofilm
  • consumes organic matter and nutrients, converting them into simpler
  • forms. The treated water then flows out, and sloughed-off biofilm
  • and solids are removed in a clarifier.
  • [K] / [CO4]

questions.question: Write the mode of transmission of infant botulism. / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Write the mode of transmission of infant botulism.
  • Infant botulism is transmitted when a baby ingests Clostridium
  • botulinum spores, which can come from contaminated soil, dust, or
  • honey. These spores germinate in the infant's immature digestive
  • system, multiply, and release a toxin that affects the nervous system.
  • Honey is a particularly well-known source of contamination for
  • infants under one year old.
  • [K] / [CO4]

questions.question: Write an analytical method to determine quality of drinking water. / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Write an analytical method to determine quality of drinking water.
  • The Most Probable Number (MPN) test for coliforms involves serial
  • dilution of a water sample and inoculating multiple tubes of a
  • selective medium like lactose broth with measured volumes of each
  • dilution. After incubation, a positive result is indicated by gas
  • bubbles and acid production in the tubes, which is often detected by
  • bubble in an inverted Durham tube and a color change from red to
  • yellow in the medium. The number of positive tubes at each dilution
  • is then used in conjunction with a standard statistical table to
  • estimate the coliform count per 100 mL of the original sample.
  • [K] / [CO4]

  • cooking. Potable water is vital for health because it prevents
  • waterborne diseases like cholera and dysentery, and is essential for
  • numerous bodily functions including regulating body temperature,
